Findings
  LOW      MAIL-MTASTS-001  MTA-STS not deployed
           hosted.example does not publish MTA-STS; senders may deliver mail over unauthenticated or
           plaintext connections.
           → Publish an MTA-STS policy (start with mode: testing and TLS-RPT) so that senders
             require authenticated TLS when delivering to your MX hosts.
           https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8461
  INFO     MAIL-DKIM-016  DKIM selectors taken from provider defaults
           hosted.example: DKIM keys were found under the documented default selectors of Google
           Workspace (google). Other selectors cannot be enumerated from DNS and were not audited.
           No DKIM key was found under the documented default selectors of SendGrid (s1, s2); the
           domain may use custom selectors, or DKIM signing may not be enabled for it there. Amazon
           SES (Easy DKIM) generates random selectors for each domain; they are shown in the SES
           console.
           https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6376#section-3.1
  INFO     MAIL-MX-013  MX hosts are reachable over IPv4 only
           hosted.example: None of the MX hosts publish AAAA records; IPv6-only senders cannot
           deliver mail.
           https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5321#section-5.1
  INFO     MAIL-MX-014  Single MX host
           hosted.example: All mail is handled by a single MX host (aspmx.l.google.com). Consider a
           backup exchanger if the provider does not already offer redundancy behind that name.
           https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5321#section-5.1
  INFO     MAIL-TLSRPT-001  TLS-RPT not configured
           hosted.example does not request SMTP TLS reports, so TLS delivery failures to its MX
           hosts go unnoticed.
           https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8460#section-3
